blocks.markdown: Covered persons must maintain accounts **only in the true and full name** of the account owner or holder. **Anonymous accounts, accounts under fictitious names, and all other similar accounts are absolutely prohibited.** Numbered accounts are not allowed **except non-checking numbered accounts**, and CTRs/STRs involving non-checking numbered accounts must still contain the **true name of the account holder**. Supervising Authorities may conduct **annual testing** solely to determine the existence and true identity of such accounts. In plain English: an account cannot be opened under a fake identity or kept anonymous; the narrow non-checking-numbered-account exception still requires identifying the real holder in reports.

**Cross-reference discrepancy:** the syllabus also cites Rule 2, Section 1(1)(n), but in the January 2021 amended IRR, Rule 2, Section 1(n) is the definition of “Beneficiary,” while the operative prohibited-account rule is **Rule 17**. Check whether the syllabus intended a different subparagraph or a different IRR version.

Covered persons must conduct CDD to **(a) identify the customer, its agents and beneficial owners; (b) determine the risk posed by each customer; (c) establish, maintain, close or terminate the account or business relationship; and (d) assess the level of monitoring**. The measures are: **(a) customer identification, (b) customer verification, (c) identification and verification of agents, (d) beneficial ownership verification, (e) determination of the purpose of the relationship, and (f) ongoing monitoring**. Covered persons must examine the background and purpose of **complex, unusually large, or unusual-pattern transactions with no apparent economic or lawful purpose** and other possibly suspicious transactions, conduct **enhanced due diligence (EDD)** where risks are higher, and — if unable to comply with relevant CDD measures — **refuse to open the account, commence relations, or perform the transaction, or terminate the relationship**, filing an STR if warranted.

In plain English: CDD is **not just asking for an ID once**. It includes verifying the customer, identifying representatives and true owners, understanding why the relationship exists, monitoring activity over time, and taking stronger steps when risk is high. If required checks cannot be completed, the institution may have to refuse or terminate the relationship and file a report when warranted.
**Glossary — Customer Due Diligence:** identify/verify the customer, agents, and beneficial owners; understand the purpose and monitor ongoing activity.
